requirements.requirement: Configure node1 as the gateway between node4/WAN, node3/LAN, and node2/DMZ.
requirements.summary: The zone links were mapped directly; node1 has the final WAN, LAN, and DMZ addresses with IPv4 forwarding enabled, while each endpoint routes remote-zone traffic through node1.

requirements.requirement: Serve infraset-dmz from node2 on port 8080.
requirements.summary: The enabled, active service listens specifically on 10.20.20.2:8080 and directly returns the expected content.

requirements.requirement: Publish only the DMZ service to WAN clients through node1 on port 8443.
requirements.summary: A WAN request to node1:8443 returned HTTP 200, and PF state showed translation to node2:8080. The final ruleset contains the corresponding redirect; bounded probes confirmed gateway ports 22, 80, 443, and 8080 and direct DMZ bypass access were blocked.

requirements.requirement: Allow LAN clients to access node2 directly on port 8080.
requirements.summary: Node3 received HTTP 200 directly from 10.20.20.2:8080; PF state and the exercised LAN pass-rule counter corroborate the routed connection.

requirements.requirement: Protect the LAN from WAN- and DMZ-initiated connections.
requirements.summary: A live LAN TCP target was established immediately before testing. Connections initiated from both WAN and DMZ timed out over routes through node1, and the matching all-protocol PF block rules each recorded packets from those tests.

overall_summary: All five material network outcomes are satisfied by direct final-state and traffic evidence. Node1 routes the three zones, the DMZ service works through the required LAN and WAN paths, alternative WAN access is blocked, and WAN/DMZ initiation toward LAN is denied. Operational hygiene is reduced by the new node3 SSH failure and leftover node1 diagnostics.
limitations: No reboot or service-restart transition was captured, so persistence beyond the observed runtime is supported by configuration and enablement but not directly tested.
WAN exclusivity was supported by the active PF ruleset and bounded negative probes, not an exhaustive all-port and all-protocol scan.
The lifecycle collector could not assess failed services or package-manager health on the FreeBSD-based OPNsense node.

operational_hygiene.summary: The required service and package state remained healthy, but executor-period hygiene was materially degraded on node3: its previously listening SSH endpoint ended with both ssh.service and ssh.socket failed and no port 22 listener. Node1 also retained its configuration script and several packet-capture/map logs under /tmp.
